Project API Reference

Core Dashboard Backend

Minimal demo application for testing ctrlX CORE REST interactions.

This script serves as a lightweight Flask-based test client for Bosch Rexroth ctrlX CORE systems. It demonstrates how to authenticate, read Data Layer values, and change the scheduler state over HTTPS using the local controller API.

The script is intended for exploratory testing and validation workflows before production deployment.

app.change_scheduler_state(target_state: str) → bool[source]

Change the ctrlX scheduler operating state.

The function sends the exact payload structure used by the controller admin API and validates the result by reading the state back from the Data Layer.

Parameters:

target_state – One of OPERATING, SETUP or SERVICE.

Returns:

True when the requested state is confirmed, otherwise False.

Return type:

bool

app.configure_connection() → None[source]

Prompt the user for ctrlX CORE connection details.

If the user presses Enter without typing, fallback values are used: IP 192.168.1.1, username and password set to boschrexroth. The password prompt masks the input for security.

app.fetch_bearer_token() → bool[source]

Authenticate against the ctrlX CORE Identity Manager.

Retrieves a valid bearer token and stores it in the shared HTTP session. This token is then used for subsequent requests to the ctrlX Data Layer and scheduler endpoints.

Returns:

True if authentication succeeds, otherwise False.

Return type:

bool

app.main() → None[source]

Run the interactive ctrlX CORE test console.

The function establishes the controller connection, authenticates, and then loops through the available Data Layer actions until the user exits.

app.read_datalayer_value(path: str) → dict | None[source]

Read a value from a specific ctrlX Data Layer node.

Parameters:

path – The node path, for example scheduler/admin/state.

Returns:

Parsed JSON payload returned by the controller, or None when the request fails.

Return type:

dict | None

app.show_menu() → str[source]

Display the interactive CLI menu and return the selected option.

Returns:

User input representing the requested action.

Return type:

str

Snap Installation Automation

ctrlX CORE App (Snap) Deployment Automation Script.

This module provides a robust command-line interface to automate the installation and management of Snap applications on Bosch Rexroth ctrlX CORE devices via the REST API, featuring highly robust, API-based state transition and upload handling.

Source: Gemini 3.6 Flash Edited by: Silas Kuschke

install_snap.change_scheduler_state(target_state: str) → bool[source]

Request a change of the scheduler operating state.

install_snap.configure_connection() → None[source]

Prompt the user for ctrlX CORE connection details.

The values are stored in the global configuration dictionary and can later be reused for authentication and package installation requests.

install_snap.fetch_bearer_token() → bool[source]

Authenticate against the Identity Manager and obtain a bearer token.

The token is written into the shared HTTP session so that subsequent installation and Data Layer requests can be authorized automatically.

Returns:

True when authentication succeeds, otherwise False.

Return type:

bool

install_snap.get_datalayer_node_value(node_path: str) → any[source]

Generic function to read a value from any Data Layer node.

install_snap.get_scheduler_state() → str[source]

Retrieve the current Scheduler operating state from the Data Layer.

install_snap.get_task_status(task_id: str) → dict | None[source]

Retrieve the status of a background package manager task.

install_snap.install_snap(snap_path: str) → bool[source]

Uploads the Snap and monitors the installation task.

install_snap.main() → None[source]

Execute the full automated app installation workflow.

install_snap.wait_for_scheduler_state(target_state: str, timeout_seconds: int = 60) → bool[source]

Poll the Scheduler operating state until it reaches the target state.

install_snap.wait_for_system_and_scheduler_ready(timeout_seconds: int = 180) → bool[source]

Polls ‘system/admin/busy’ and ‘scheduler/admin/state/switching’. Waits until both are False. Uses ‘is not True’ for robust backwards-compatibility if nodes are not supported.

install_snap.wait_for_task_completion(task_id: str, timeout_seconds: int = 300) → bool[source]

Poll the task status endpoint until the installation task is complete.

License Installation Automation

ctrlX CORE License Deployment Automation Script.

This module provides a command-line interface to automate the installation of license capability responses (.bin files) on Bosch Rexroth ctrlX CORE devices via the REST API. It supports single or multi-device installation, secure credentials storage, and automatic 13-digit serial number retrieval.

Source: Gemini 3.6 Flash Edited by: Silas Kuschke

Authenticates and stores the Bearer token in the global session.

install_license.fetch_serial_number(ip: str) → str | None[source]

Retrieves the 13-digit serial number from the ctrlX CORE.

install_license.get_single_core_input() → dict[source]

Prompts the user for single-device connection details.

A dictionary containing saved IP configurations and credentials.

Main execution flow.

Saves a CORE configuration securely to the .env file.

install_license.upload_license(ip: str, file_path: str) → bool[source]

Uploads the license file using the confirmed PUT method and correct endpoint.

This function parses the server’s change report to dynamically identify which licenses were added or if the license was already processed.

Parameters:

  • ip (str) – The IP address of the target ctrlX CORE.

  • file_path (str) – The local path to the .bin license file.

Returns:

True if the upload was successful, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool
